title: Dedicated Pool Elasticity: Playbook and Launch Cadence
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Purpose: Define an operational playbook and launch cadence for elastic behavior of dedicated GPU pools. This ticket captures the product decisions, rollout milestones, measurable SLOs, and cross-team coordination required to ship predictable autoscaling for Dedicated customers.

Scope: build a first production-grade elasticity mode that supports: scheduled reservation windows, demand-driven horizontal scaling across reserved pools, and a predictive burst layer for short-lived traffic spikes. Excludes long-term billing changes and advanced predictive ML model training (separate follow-up).

Objectives: (1) Enable customers to set elasticity policies per-pool (min/max nodes, target utilization bands, latency SLOs), (2) Provide Safe Rollout: canary/percent rollout with automatic rollback on key regressions, (3) Surface unit economics in Console (per-token cost delta vs baseline), (4) Verify reliability with e2e stress tests and production canary on beta customers.

Key product decisions and trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive scaling vs. model cache warmup: faster scale ups reduce latency but risk higher per-token cost and cold KV cache misses. We recommend a hybrid approach: maintain a small warm pool for hot models + rapid burst workers for queued requests.
- Predictive vs reactive autoscale: predictive scaling reduces tail latency at higher cost and requires historical telemetry; start with reactive (utilization + queue depth) with a planned ML-predictive pilot in cycle+2.
- Multi-tenant packing: packing increases utilization but adds noisy-neighbor risk; for initial launch restrict packing to same-tenant pools or labeled low-priority workloads.

Success metrics: 
- Latency P95 for provisioned traffic remains within target (<= 350ms for small LLMs) during scaling events.
- Dedicated pool CPU/GPU utilization stabilized to target band 60-75% within 3 minutes of autoscale event.
- Cost delta for beta customers <= 12% above static reserved baseline for equivalent throughput.
- No more than 2 regressions requiring rollback during rollout window.

Deliverables: 
- Product spec & policy editor UI in Console (PRD: link).
- Autoscale orchestration service with policy primitives (min/max/target/priority).
- Canary rollout plan + health gates and automated rollback.
- E2E chaos/stress test suite and a Grafana dashboard for rollout monitoring.
- Beta onboarding docs and runbook for Support/CS.

Operational constraints: must integrate with existing cost-tracking pipeline, support RBAC for policy edits, and respect customer isolation for Private deployments.

Links to artifacts: PRD, design mocks, GitHub, dashboards and initial customer notes are in the links field.
acceptance_criteria: Policy editor in Console allows creating/editing per-pool elasticity policies (min, max, target, priority) and saving to release channel.
Autoscale controller implements reactive rules (utilization + queue depth) and exposes metrics for decisions in telemetry pipeline.
Canary rollout mechanism supports gradual percent rollout, health gates (latency, error rate, scaling success), and automated rollback within 15 minutes of breach.
E2E stress tests simulate burst traffic and validate P95 and utilization SLOs across three model archetypes.
Cost telemetry surfaces per-pool per-hour cost delta in Console within 1 hour of change and is tested end-to-end.
Beta customers (minimum 3) onboarded with runbook and observed for two weeks with no critical availability incidents attributable to autoscale behavior.
milestones: 2026-03-31: Backend autoscale controller MVP complete (internal testing)
2026-04-22: Canary rollout tooling + automated rollback implemented
2026-04-30: E2E stress test validation and beta customer selection
2026-05-10: Begin beta rollout to selected customers
2026-05-15: Beta evaluation complete and go/no-go decision for wider release
risks: Cold KV cache after rapid scale-up leading to temporary latency spikes.
Underestimated cost for predictive/autoscale behavior causing negative customer economics.
Controller oscillation (thrashing) if policies are too aggressive or telemetry noisy.
Edge cases in Private/VPC deployments where network provisioning delays slow scale-up.
Operator confusion without clear Console defaults and recommended policy templates.
